A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DESIGNER pipeline and DLR datasets. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison; the relocated prompts and design-logic examples were matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original dataset analyses, supervised fine-tuning results, scaling experiments, source-quality comparisons, and component ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds a data-quality audit, a full-scale ablation, and mathematical benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: The extraction models, graph deduplication, top-five retrieval, LLM selection, question generation, and response synthesis remain unchanged, as do the synthesis prompts and Algorithm 1. The added backfilling explanation documents preprocessing detail; GPT-5.1 is introduced for evaluation, not as a synthesis component.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds model evaluations on GSM8K and MATH-500, extending testing to dedicated mathematical answer-generation benchmarks. GSM8K previously appeared only in difficulty analysis. The training corpora, 75-discipline coverage, and existing multidisciplinary evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The four dataset baselines and official Llama/Qwen comparison models are retained. The full-scale ablation reuses the existing 'w/o Design Logic' method at a larger scale. Appendix I extends the retained model comparisons; its cited GPT-4o score is not a newly conducted baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: GPT-5.1 judges six quality and label criteria on 10,000 randomly sampled instances. Section 5.6 adds a paired ablation at 3.04 million examples alongside the retained 304,181-example experiments. Existing SFT hyperparameters and the main zero-shot evaluation configuration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new audit directly examines answerability, design-logic alignment, label appropriateness, and reference-answer/CoT agreement, substantially extending the earlier difficulty and diversity analyses. The full-scale ablation tests whether design-logic guidance remains useful beyond the original small-sample comparison. Existing scaling, source-quality, and component analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten GPQA rollouts and report mean accuracy, standard deviation, and self-consistency accuracy. MATH-500 adds rows using the existing mean-plus-standard-deviation practice, without documenting its rollout count. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, training-seed information, or uncertainty-estimation procedure appear.

E6.justification: v4 adds six audit outcomes, including 96.70% answerability and 71.48% answer agreement, plus Table 15's mathematical benchmark results. Table 5 adds the full-scale ablated model's GPQA-Diamond score of 64.10±2.81 against the retained DESIGNER result of 69.39±1.87. Table 4 corrects DLR-Book's MMLU-Pro value from 74.34 to 74.98. Table 3's scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The similarity-graph formulation, representative-selection algorithm, retrieval equation, and Appendix G diversity definitions are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are subsequently added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract newly emphasizes controllable question types and difficulty levels, while the contribution statement and conclusion explicitly claim structured control over difficulty and diversity. The central contributions—the design-logic pipeline, two multidisciplinary datasets, and improved reasoning performance—remain intact.

C2.justification: v4 explains answer disagreement through open-ended questions and attributes weaker MATH-500 performance to limited mathematical data and less extensive post-training. It also discusses GSM8K saturation and newly asserts applicability to any question bank regardless of initial quality. These add qualifications and applicability arguments without replacing the main interpretations.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes from promising a dataset subset to reporting its release, and additionally reports release of the complete labeled design-logic library. v4 also supplies six audit prompts and documents lower-difficulty backfilling when harder seed questions are insufficient. This substantially expands stated reproducibility resources, although hosted availability cannot be independently established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds Brown, Gao, and Rae references supporting the source-quality discussion, and Vendrow et al. for GSM8K benchmark limitations. The query-centric/doc-centric positioning and comparisons with structurally guided synthesis research remain largely unchanged. The revised Llama 3 citation refers to the same work.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, contribution statement, conclusion, and reproducibility statement, plus terminology clarifications such as adding 'Base' to Qwen model labels. Section 4.4 and Appendix I are inserted, shifting the prompt and example appendix letters. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 15 and six boxed evaluation-prompt figures, extends Table 5 with full-scale rows, and adds totals to Table 6. Figures 5–6 receive expanded captions, and several displays move with text reflow. The existing charts, pipeline diagrams, and design-logic illustrations retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The quality audit and full-scale ablation strengthen empirical support, the Table 4 correction removes an inconsistency, and the reported resource release improves reproducibility. The added math results also expose a useful boundary: DLR-trained Qwen models trail official Qwen models on MATH-500. These gains remain limited by reliance on one LLM judge, an untested explanation for answer disagreement, and stronger claims of precise difficulty control without corresponding control experiments.
